Circle Drawer's canvas declares one virtual node per circle it paints (an author key, an AccessKit role, a non-empty name, a region in its content box), the first served app to declare virtual nodes.
Each circle then reads as a node `{owner}///{key}` in the accessibility tree, the snapshot, the diff, the UI graph, `actions`, `layout` and exploration; `click` on a circle's node acts on its circle, and a covered, off-screen, disabled or removed circle node is refused with that cause.
The canvas reading groups a canvas's draw commands under the virtual node that covers them, and a changed command reads with an identity in the reading's diff.
It adds stand checks in both layout modes and the binary-level reading of a virtual node's id and name, sweeps every committed stand pin and stated literal that reads Circle Drawer's screen, and re-verifies seven carried items (label region, virtual-node `covered`, handler coverage of a virtual node, the lint reading no virtual node, a Windows unused-import warning).

body: Circle Drawer's drawing area changes from one named canvas node read as pixels only to a canvas whose circles each read as a node of their own; the rule that names that drawing area as one canvas node is what this changes.

Each circle node's id takes the reserved separator form `{owner}///{key}`; a circle has no id of its own, so its key, role and name are open choices, and every interactive node must carry a non-empty name.
A circle's region must lie inside its canvas's content box (a region outside it is refused); a circle near the canvas edge spills the box, which the declaration must handle.

Circle nodes appear in the accessibility tree, the snapshot and its text form, the snapshot diff, the UI graph (one node per snapshot node, carrying no values), the actions answer and its fields, layout and exploration, as served for this app.

Click on a circle's node is a synthetic primary click at its centre that acts on its circle, and the diff names the node; the click refusal causes covered, off-screen, disabled and removed apply to a circle node and are read on the stand.
A virtual node reads covered only by an element over its region's centre, never by another virtual node of its canvas; overlapping circles put this rule to the test and it is re-verified here.

Handler coverage lists no handler for a virtual node and counts a click on one as its canvas's own listener under the canvas's id; Circle Drawer's canvas carries an onclick listener, so the coverage answer for it is re-verified.
The lint reads no virtual node: overlapping circles must raise no overlap, clip or off-screen finding on a declared region, and the stand must still read no lint finding at boot.
A canvas label's region (read against the content box cut by clip, layer or mask paths and the element's clip region, or as the shape or virtual node under it) is a carried question re-verified here.

The canvas reading groups draw commands under the virtual node covering them and gives a changed command an identity in its diff, where today a changed command reads as one line removed and one added; naming a node's id in the canvas answer is a crossing change.
The binary-level reading: the socket host's answer, the command line's stdout and a cold-agent live run each carry a virtual node's id and name, read on the binary.

Every committed stand pin reading Circle Drawer's screen moves and is swept, literal pins included: the cross-OS digest tables, the canvas commands table, the canvas lint, non-lean task and Circle Drawer canvas checks, and the capability statement's sizes and counts.
Stand checks of the circle nodes run in both layout modes.
The Windows build must warn no unused import in the virtual-nodes test file, checked by a cargo check of the tests for the Windows GNU target.
Evidence holds no raw log with a temp or home path; a control enters with its red reading; a probe worktree lives outside target/ and is not deleted by a plan step.

body: Keyboard rows (Tab order, Enter and Space activation, focus moves and focus fixup, Cells grid and CRUD list keys): keyboard reach of the circles is the next entry's, not built here.
Single and multiple select, open select list, list box and range input rows (their keys, rows, colours, events and snapshot readings): Circle Drawer's circles are no form control.

ARIA attribute reads and ARIA state rows (aria-checked, aria-pressed, aria-selected, aria-invalid, aria-expanded, aria-level, aria-describedby): a virtual node's role and name are declared by the canvas widget, not read from ARIA attributes.
Password masking, file input value and IME rows: no text entry is touched.

Platform adapter and assistive-technology reach rows, and the keyboard or assistive-technology drag-and-drop absence: the stand builds no platform adapter, and the binary reading here is over the socket host, command line and cold-agent pipe.

body: A virtual node now crosses on a served app: each circle's id, role and name leave by every carrier the virtual node crossing ratifies — snapshot, diff, graph, actions, layout, exploration report, socket reply, command line stdout and MCP result — and by no other.

The stable element id's virtual-node form `{owner}///{key}`: the circle's author key must be stable across reads, unique within its canvas and hold no process-local handle or NodeId, though a circle has no id of its own.

Declared virtual nodes are validated by a closed refusal set: a circle near the canvas edge whose region spills the content box meets the region-outside refusal, an empty name is refused; the declaration must stay inside those bounds.

A click on a virtual node passes the one target check shared with the actions read, and refusals keep the fixed order and closed cause set (covered, off-screen, disabled, stale, not-found), each holding nothing the call supplied and logged by cause name only.
A virtual node reads covered only by an element over its region's centre, never by another virtual node of its canvas (CARRY 3); overlapping circles put this rule on the stand.

The canvas answer changes: grouping draw commands under a virtual node puts a node's id into the canvas answer, a crossing change to the canvas content crossing, which today holds no virtual node; a changed command's identity in the line diff is new content in that answer.
The canvas answer, graph, actions and layout answers are kept whole in kept checks; a virtual node's id and name in them fall under the kept check's owner-only, uncommitted rule.

The lint reads no virtual node (CARRY 7) and its findings hold closed content only; a canvas label's region read as the shape or virtual node under it (CARRY 2) touches the canvas label crossing in a lint finding.
Handler coverage of a virtual node (CARRY 6): no handler of its own, a click counted as the canvas's own listener under the canvas's id; the coverage answer line carries no user data.
A circle's accessible name is an accessible name: it leaves only by ratified exits and is kept out of logs, as stable ids are; the command span and tool_call span hold no content.
The diff and snapshot text carry the node's id field, name field and state words; a click's diff names the acted circle through the diff node keys.

CARRY 4's cold-agent live run carries the screen and canvas answers, now holding circle node ids and names, to the provider; its events and logs stay run metadata only, its recordings owner-only and its raw transcript and server output unprinted.
Evidence from the live and binary-level runs enters with no raw log carrying a temp or home path and no credentials; the recording or state directory is never named.
The windows build fix (CARRY 5) is checked by a locked cargo check of the test crate for the windows target.

Committed stand pins and literal pins that read Circle Drawer's screen are swept: the cross-OS digest tables, the canvas commands table, the lint and non-lean checks, and the capability statement's sizes and counts move with the circles becoming nodes.
The driver session socket and the MCP server answers stay within their size bounds when Circle Drawer's answers grow by its circle nodes; the actions answer stays unpaged and the graph answer paged.

body: Authentication and authorization: CI tokens, publish guards and the absence of application auth are untouched by a canvas declaring nodes.
Outbound network rules — script and sub-resource fetches, per-host limits, CORS and same-origin, request timeouts, TLS, external navigation schemes: Circle Drawer's circles load nothing.
Select lists, range inputs, password and file masking, optgroups and select keyboards: Circle Drawer's canvas holds none of these controls.
HTML, CSS and SVG parsing rules — invalid declarations, selectors, @import and iframe nesting, font-face sources, inline SVG serialization: the chunk parses no new markup.
Browser history, cookies, the HTTP cache, the history database and SQL placeholders: no served app storage is touched.
CI secrets, signing material, publishing and the WPT workflows: the chunk adds no release or WPT job.
JavaScript opt-in, the dioxus-native JS evaluation and the CDP devtools server: the seven_guis app runs no script and the devtools feature is not built.
Keyboard reach of canvas virtual nodes and virtual nodes of rotated or scaled canvases: they belong to later entries, not built here.

body: The reserved owner-key id form of a virtual node (owner, three slashes, key) as Circle Drawer's circle nodes carry it in every read: element ids, snapshot nodes, the UI graph answer, the actions answer and the layout answer.

Click on a circle's virtual node: the acting call result and its diff name the circle node; the refusal causes covered, off-screen, disabled, not-found and stale apply to a circle node with their fixed order and printed form, and a refusal changes nothing.
A virtual node reads covered only by an element over its region's centre, never by another virtual node of its canvas — overlapping circles put this rule on the stand (CARRY 3).

The canvas command line verb and the canvas reading: draw commands grouped under the virtual node that covers them, and a changed command read with an identity in the line diff (CARRY 1); naming a node's id in the canvas answer changes that answer's shape.

Handler coverage over a canvas handler: a virtual node carries no handler of its own, so the coverage line lists none for it and counts a click on it as the canvas's own listener under the canvas's id; Circle Drawer's canvas carries onclick (CARRY 6).

The lint reads no virtual node: no overlap, clip or off-screen finding on a declared region, held by the guard that the lint holds no virtual node, now on Circle Drawer's overlapping circles (CARRY 7); the lint's defect kinds and finding order stay as they are for elements.
The canvas lint's label region: a label read as the shape or the virtual node under it, against the content box cut by each clip, layer or mask path (CARRY 2).
A declared region must lie inside the canvas's content box (a region outside it is refused), so a circle near the canvas edge bounds the region the chunk's code declares.

Binary-level reading of a virtual node's id and name through the session host's answer, the command line's stdout, the MCP server's tool result and the cold-agent pipe (CARRY 4), each by the package's own binary.
